messages:
Anya K: Quick heads-up — during r2-int8 onboarding for billing-invoke the model is producing malformed structured outputs for the function call payloads in ~12% of the eval set. Mostly trailing commas / missing closing braces, sometimes stray text after JSON.
Ben L: ugh. paste one raw example? truncated or extra tokens?
Anya K: raw snippet below (from a single turn):
```
{"action": "charge_customer", "params": {"customer_id": "cus_123", "amount": 49.99},
```
(then newline and "thank you" text appended)
Carlos M: interesting — that looks like truncation + extra generation. could be max_new_tokens or kv-cache alignment after quantization change. Did you see same on fp16 canary?
Anya K: fp16 was clean. This only shows up on the int8-converted variant and only when batch size >= 4 in our local serving harness.
Ben L: sounds like batching/kv boundary corruption. can you run with continuous_batching disabled and repro? also try with `--max_new_tokens 128` vs 64.
Anya K: repro with batching disabled reduces failure rate to ~1.5%. with bigger max_new_tokens the failures still exist but different morphology (extra trailing html-like text).
Eva S: throwing a quick parse harness at it now. snippet of my probe: 
```python
# probe parse check
from jsonschema import Draft7Validator
payload = model.generate(prompt)
try:
  parsed = json.loads(payload)
except Exception as e:
  print('PARSE_ERR', payload[:200])
```
I saw an output where the model emitted two JSON blobs concatenated with plain text in between — looks like generation didn't stop after closing brace.
Carlos M: that points to stop-token handling + eos scoring in quantized runtime. kernel selection may change token logits for eos. we recently changed soft-eos threshold for r2 quant.
Ben L: can we try temp=0.0 and set explicit stop sequences in the routing policy for billing-invoke? Also enable postprocess-rescue step: attempt strict parse, then run a lightweight heuristic repair (wrap in [...], take first balanced JSON, simple regex to remove trailing words).
Anya K: I ran temp=0.0 and stop token `\n\n` — failure dropped to 6% but not gone. heuristic repair catches ~80% of failures but we need to decide whether that counts as acceptable for onboarding.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment r2-int8 -> staging completed (pods: 6).
Eva S: I pushed a small eval PR with more diagnostics (link: https://git.company/repo/pull/412). It adds token-level trace and a quick levenshtein filter comparing generated JSON to expected shape.
Ben L: +1 for token traces. we should also add a lightweight lint in the inference pipeline: if parse fails, emit structured failure reason (truncated / concatenated / extra-text) and attach top-K token probs around the closing brace. That will help root-cause.
Carlos M: long-term fix likely in quant kernel/eos calibrations — but as a stopgap: 1) disallow batching >1 for billing-invoke on r2-int8 in Dedicated, 2) enable strict stop sequences, 3) add parse-repair fallback and failure telemetry.
Anya K: agree. I'll open a ticket to block batching for that route and enable the postprocess repair. Also adding an eval slice for concatenated-json errors.
Eva S: quick note — for the eval harness I observed failures spike when conversation context has long system messages (kv-cache usage). maybe prefix length interacts with kv offsets after quant kernels. I'll add a slice for long-prefix cases.
Ben L: thanks, team. let's aim to have mitigation toggles in staging by EOD and a follow-up postmortem on the exact token-level failure mode once traces are in. :thumbsup:
Anya K: filing the mitigation PRs now, will ping for review.
Carlos M: ping me once token traces are live, I'll correlate with kernel selection logs.
Eva S: I also dropped three failing examples into the eval bucket under /datasets/qa-onboarding/json-failures for auditing.
Anya K: perfect — thanks everyone.
